signal.reasoning: I can understand the economics well enough to see an excellent cash-generating business: margins are high and steady, free cash flow per share exceeds earnings per share, and book value per share has risen. Those figures suggest a moat and sound capital allocation, though four trailing periods cannot prove either will last a decade; debt is manageable, but the current ratio leaves little cushion. At 37.5 times earnings, I would want more assurance of durable growth before calling this a fair price, so I would admire the business without buying it on these facts alone.
